body: Ace Combat X: Skies of Deception is Namco Bandai and Access Games' PSP aerial combat game, first released in North America on 23 October 2006. The player leads Gryphus Squadron of the Aurelian Air Force through a campaign of air and ground attacks. It is the series' first PSP entry, carrying its mixture of accessible flight, mission briefings and military fiction into a portable format. A small aircraft remains part of a larger conflict, with the player choosing how to approach an operation before bringing the selected weapons and manoeuvres to bear on its targets.

Campaign progress unlocks operations for Free Mission, allowing the player to revisit a known objective for a better rank or more points. Those rewards can purchase aircraft and equipment, connecting a successful sortie to the options available later. The player learns which threats deserve attention first and how an approach can leave more room for the next turn. Air targets and ground installations ask for different positioning, so the same aircraft must be understood in relation to the work ahead. Familiarity makes the operation more deliberate rather than simply easier to survive.

Masanori Kato directed and designed the game, with Tamio Kanaji writing its story. The music is credited to Akira Yamasaki, Hitoshi Akiyama, Seiji Koike and Maiko Iuchi, with Yuji Takenouchi supervising after other commitments prevented him from composing. Japanese and European releases followed shortly after North America in 2006. Multiplayer adds another use for the aircraft beyond the campaign. The handheld entry preserves the series' central relationship between pilot, equipment and objective, giving players a complete aerial-combat journey that can be carried away from the television.
